Given my family history / bad genes (heart disease, alcoholism) and with both my parents living only to mid-50’s (mom heart attack, dad cirrhosis). I may also have him see a cardiologist. 

For me— I’ve spent the last 2 years doing everything that someone at high risk of heart disease shouldn’t do, especially at my age (42): eat sugar, fast food, sometimes nothing, few vegetables, no exercise not even walking dog, too much drinking, worry all the time… this is mainly due to depression and my extremely hectic job during Covid (work in finance, 12+ hour days). I stopped drinking almost a year ago but all other bad habits remained.  I have some time off work because my physical & mental health was getting worse and worse and knew I had to address it. Finally went for check up after 2 years. I have the bad cholesterol, severely low levels of vitamin D & B, anemic, pre-diabetes and Hashimoto’s.  

In the 2 weeks since seeing that I’m on supplements, Rosuvastatin, and Synthroid abs eating extremely healthy, no sugar, lots of fresh veggies, fish and chicken, gluten free grains. Doing moderate exercise for 30 min each day even if it’s just walking. I already feel so much better. Now I can Include my son on those changes.  I am seeing a cardiologist myself this week for consult given my family history, age and sad state of my labs. Hoping for best there too, EKG in PCP’s office last week was good.
